answer: To resist Sybil attacks in an agent economy, credential-stake mechanisms offer concrete defense. Agents lock real-world assets—such as timber—as collateral to earn trading privileges. A fake identity must deposit these stakes, instantly transferring them to the victim or burning them. A gale of Sybil attempts thus faces astronomical capital requirements. The brief reward feels like a comet, fading before attackers profit, as the prohibitive entry cost prevents mass identity farming.
